title: The Captured Images thumbnail rail cannot be scrolled with an ordinary mouse wheel and has no scrollbar
summary: Confirmed at the cited location. The rail was a bare horizontal ListView.builder with the default desktop ScrollBehavior, so a vertical wheel notch went to the page and the trailing frames of a long night were reachable only by shift+wheel, which nothing advertised. Fixed the cause using the pattern skotiq_ui's AdaptiveTabBar already uses: a Listener maps PointerScrollEvent.dy onto an owned ScrollController (horizontal deltas are left to the Scrollable so nothing double-scrolls), and the list is wrapped in Scrollbar(thumbVisibility: true). The rail keeps its exact height — the scrollbar's 10px comes out of the list's own bottom padding — so the loading and error placeholders in session_tab, which use the same kAnalyticsThumbnailRailHeight constant, do not jump when the data arrives.

title: Captured Images thumbnails are inert — tapping a frame does nothing anywhere in Analytics
summary: Confirmed: ImageThumbnailStrip declared onImageTap and neither of its two call sites (session_tab.dart, session_detail_dialog.dart) passed one, so a left click — the gesture everyone tries first — did nothing, and the only per-frame affordance was an unadvertised long-press/right-click menu. Rather than wiring a handler at each call site (which leaves the next caller inert again), the strip now opens its own frame inspector when no handler is supplied, and a supplied handler still wins. Built FrameDetailDialog: enlarged preview from the same backend thumbnail the rail already fetches, a metadata table from the row (exposure, filter, gain/offset, binning, sensor temp, HFR, stars, guiding RMS, focuser position, mount altitude, solved position, pixel scale, zero point, path), the rejection reason when the frame is rejected, and an accept/reject action that goes through imagingRecordsRepositoryProvider so it reaches the host in remote mode. Solved RA is printed as h:m:s via CoordinateParser because the column is HOURS. The thumbnail loader was extracted to frame_thumbnail_loader.dart so the rail and the inspector cannot disagree about whether a frame is viewable. NOT done: the finding suggested opening ImageGraderDialog — that is a bulk rule-based grader over a whole session and is the wrong thing to open from a single frame.

title: Equipment Stats: half of the tab is permanently "Not tracked"
summary: Partly real, and only partly fixable without new instrumentation — so I fixed the part that was a lie and left the rest. Meridian Flips IS recorded: every sequence run persists a stats blob carrying `meridianFlips` (sequence_runs.statsJson, parsed by ParsedRunStats, already printed by the Morning Report and the run history), and the tab hardcoded 'Not tracked' beside it. That row now totals the recorded count across all runs, via sequenceRunsProvider so it works on a slave over the network too, with a malformed or legacy blob contributing zero instead of taking the tab down. The other five are NOT derivable: I checked and there is no slew count, no tracking-time accumulator, and no focuser-step counter anywhere in the schema; guide_rms_history keys on a TEXT session id and stores per-sample RMS with a nullable exposure, so 'Total Guide Time' could only be inferred, and 'Star Lost Events' is not recorded at all. Wiring those means new columns and new write paths through the mount ops, the focuser ops and the PHD2 bridge — see the separate needs-decision entry.

title: Science tab defaults to the newest session even when it has no science data
summary: Confirmed by reading the chain: the tab fell back to latestScienceSessionProvider, which answers 'newest session holding LIGHT frames' — a different question, so two test frames shot after a photometry night win, and the tab opens on '0 of N solved' with the never-started empty state while the calibrated night sits one row down in a dropdown. The rule chosen dominates rather than trades off: when the newest session HAS science both rules agree, and when it does not the old one shows nothing usable. Added ImagesDao.getSessionIdsWithSolvedFrames and ScienceDao.getSessionIdsWithPhotometry, plus latestScienceProductSessionProvider, which orders candidates by allSessionsProvider (newest first) so 'most recent' means the same thing here as in the session picker beside it. It slots in as: manual pick -> live -> newest with a science product -> newest with light frames -> newest at all, so nothing that used to resolve now resolves to less. The tab's own 'Analysing <name>' bar still names the session, so the choice is visible.

title: Science report timestamps are printed without a timezone, so a shared report is ambiguous by up to a day
summary: Confirmed at science_report_exporter.dart. Drift hands session start/end back as LOCAL DateTimes, so '**Started:** ...' printed local wall time in ISO-8601 shape with no offset and no Z, a few lines above a footer that carries a Z and a light-curve block explicitly labelled '(UTC)'. One convention now: a _utcStamp helper converts to UTC and the fields are labelled '**Started (UTC):**' / '**Ended (UTC):**'. Only the Session block was wrong — the light-curve block already called .toUtc() before formatting.

title: Every science rung sheet is a dead end: it names the blocker but gives no button to clear it
summary: Confirmed: the sheet's locked branch rendered only 'Got it', even though the ladder card already hands it an onCta and the app already knows where each prerequisite is satisfied. The sheet now takes an optional unlockLabel/onUnlock and renders it beside 'Got it' for a locked rung. Deliberately NOT the rung's own CTA: rung 5's CTA opens the export hub and that rung is locked precisely because there is nothing to export, so routing there would replace one dead end with another. All three lockable prerequisites (track a star, gather ten points, record something exportable) are satisfied in the photometry section, so the unlock action is a single honest 'Go to photometry' that fires the card's existing onJumpToPhotometry. Never-locked rungs (measure, track) get no unlock action, keyed off the same _prerequisiteFor map that decides whether a prerequisite is shown at all.

title: 3D Surface Explorer has no axes, no colour scale and no numbers, so the plot cannot be read
summary: Confirmed: the painter drew 25 coloured circles and nothing else, so a 2% uniformity spread and a 40% one rendered identically and a red corner could not be mapped onto a physical adjustment. Three additions, all from data already on screen. (1) Corner labels drawn ON the surface: the four grid corners are projected and tagged r0·c0 / r0·c4 / r4·c0 / r4·c4 — indices, not TL/TR, because the surface can be orbited so a fixed legend would be wrong half the time, and because tile_row/tile_col are provably the image row/column order (native/.../api/imaging.rs builds them from the y/x loops). (2) A colour bar under the plot with the ramp's own 5th/95th-percentile ends, the median, the true min-max range and the layer's unit where the producer provably writes one (% for clip_low/clip_high, ADU for background, mag for residual_mag, px for fwhm/hfr; the ratios are left unitless rather than guessed). (3) Tap-to-read: the projection was extracted into projectSurfaceTiles so the hit test resolves against the same points the painter drew, the nearest marker within 18px is ringed and its tile and value printed; a tap that lands nowhere clears the readout instead of reporting a tile nobody aimed at, and changing layer clears it so one layer's value is never printed under another's name. Also shrank the plot as the finding asked: it was a full-width 16:9 box that ran to ~450px of mostly empty space on a desktop column and, once the scale bar was added, pushed the controls out of the card — it now follows the width up to a 300px cap.

title: Period Analysis states the same period in three different units in one card (min, days, hours)
summary: Confirmed at all three cited locations. _formatPeriod was a private method on the panel state while each painter carried its own inline formatting, so the headline said '20.0 min', the Lomb-Scargle marker 'P=0.014d' and the BLS marker 'P=0.33h' for one peak. Promoted the formatter to a library-level formatPeriodLabel (the painters are `part of` the panel), and both markers now go through named periodogramPeakLabel / blsPeakLabel helpers built on it, so the markers read exactly like the headline. Axes keep their natural units as the finding asked, but the BLS x-axis title now says 'Period (h / d, log)' instead of a bare 'Period' over ticks that switch unit mid-axis; the LS axis was already labelled 'Frequency (1/day)'.

title: Image grader shows the same value 'off' with the slider thumb at opposite ends of two adjacent tracks
summary: The defect class is real but the reported repro is not the path that produces it, so read this before believing the screenshot. With NULL fwhm and NULL eccentricity both rows fall to their synthetic ranges ([0,12] and [0,1]) and BOTH park at the top — I could not reproduce a left-pinned FWHM that way. The real cause is a degenerate range: when every frame carries the same value, rangeMin == rangeMax, the track is widened to rangeMin+1 so Material will render it, but the off value was clamped against rangeMax — i.e. to the BOTTOM of a track that runs one unit higher. Two rules with different data shapes then show the same word 'off' at opposite ends. Fixed by making the clamp follow the widened track (thresholdSliderMax / maxRuleThumbValue, now named and testable), so an off 'Max x' rule always sits at the permissive top and an off 'Min stars' rule always at the permissive bottom. Also dimmed an off rule's track to 0.45 opacity so it stops reading as a threshold in force, while staying draggable — dragging an off rule is how you switch it on, and disabling it would have taken that away.

title: Photometric Calibration Wizard's frame picker has no select-all / filter-by-altitude, so building the airmass spread it asks for means clicking through 120 identical rows
summary: Confirmed, and worse than reported: the wizard's own star-matching step REFUSES a frame whose mount altitude was never recorded (star_matching.dart throws rather than inventing X = 1.0), so a user could select 120 rows and only learn at 'Match Stars' that some of them can never contribute. The picker now shows what the fit needs and what it will refuse. Each row carries 'Alt 52.3° · X 1.26', computed through the product's one airmass model (airmassForTrueAltitude) so the list and the fit agree, and a frame with no usable altitude reads 'no recorded altitude — cannot fit' in the warning colour. Above the list: a live 'N of M selected · K unusable' count, 'Select all usable' (which takes the frames that match the filter being calibrated AND have an altitude, so it cannot hand the fit a frame it will reject) and 'Clear'. NOT done: sort-by-airmass and a 'select spread (lowest/median/highest)' picker — those are feature design rather than a defect, and the airmass column plus Select all already makes the spread visible and reachable.

title: Calibration wizard prints solved RA/Dec as bare decimals with no unit
summary: Real, and the finding's expectation was wrong in a way worth recording: it proposed 'RA 120.0000 deg', but captured_images.solved_ra is HOURS (0-24), not degrees — the plate-solve writer stores solved.raHours, the headless handler validates min:0/max:24, and star_matching reads it back as WcsSolution.raHours. The reporter's '120.0000' was seeded test data in an hours column. Rows now read 'RA 05:30:00.00  Dec +25:00:00.00' through CoordinateParser.formatRaHms / formatDecDms — the formatters skotiq_core already owns and that the MPC exporter's sexagesimal output agrees with — so the value is unambiguous and a degrees-valued seed would now be visibly out of range. The same formatting is used in the new frame inspector.

title: With no data at all, Analytics > Session invents a session card called "Quick Capture" instead of an empty state
summary: Confirmed: the standalone bucket is a real thing (frames shot outside a sequence) but it was also the fallback whenever no session was under review, so a brand-new profile opened Analytics on a named card with a duration, an exposure count and four blank charts for a night that had never happened. The bucket now renders only when it actually holds frames. Two empty states rather than one, because the two situations are different and a single message would be false in one of them: with no sessions at all it uses History's own 'No session history / Complete an imaging session to see history here' (existing l10n keys, so no new untranslated strings); with sessions on record but none selected it keeps the session picker and says 'No quick captures — choose a session above to review it', which is true and actionable where 'you have not imaged yet' would be a lie.

title: Empty-chart messages splice the axis label into the sentence, producing "No °C recorded for these frames"
summary: Confirmed at session_chart.dart. The empty state was composed from yAxisLabel, which carries units, so the four Session-tab charts read 'No HFR (px) recorded...', 'No RMS (arcsec) recorded...', 'No Focuser position (steps) recorded...' and 'No °C recorded for these frames'. SessionChart now takes an optional measurementName — a noun phrase for prose, separate from the axis caption — and the four wrappers pass 'half-flux radius', 'sensor temperature', 'guiding RMS' and 'focuser position'. It falls back to the card title rather than the axis label, so any future chart that forgets it still gets a sentence rather than a unit.

title: Three separate tutorial systems fire at once on a first run, and the second one tells the user to do what they just did
summary: Two of the three causes were already closed in this shard's working tree and I revert-verified both: (a) FirstLaunchTourDao.getStatus() maps a MISSING progress row to notStarted rather than pending, so the replay-only coach-mark tour ('Three things to set up first: equipment, a profile, and a sequence') no longer auto-fires on a fresh install on top of the wizard that just did exactly that; (b) ContextualTourPrompt suppresses itself while that coach-mark overlay is mounted. The residue I closed is the one the repro actually lands on: 'Show me on the Sequencer screen' pops the walkthrough and navigates, and the Sequencer then raised its own 'Sequencer Tour — learn how to create and run automated imaging sequences' nudge, offering a tour of the screen the walkthrough step had just explained. Added a session-scoped guidedFlowActiveProvider that the first-night walkthrough claims on open and releases only on Done / Skip forever / Close — deliberately NOT on dispose, because a deep link parks the walkthrough rather than ending it. The prompt checks the flag before showing and hides (without spending the dismissal) if a walkthrough starts while it is already up.

title: The onboarding step list marks a step complete just for visiting it
summary: Already closed in this shard's working tree; I confirmed it by revert. _StepSidebar is now a ConsumerWidget taking the live draft, and a passed step is ticked only when `draft.producedValueFor(step, siteConfigured: ...)` is true — the same question the Review screen answers. Visited-but-empty steps (a guider whose PHD2 test failed and where nothing was selected) render a dash glyph instead of a filled blue tick, with tooltips 'Configured' / 'Skipped — nothing was set' / 'Current step' / 'Not reached yet'. The observing site is read from appSettingsProvider rather than the draft because it is a global observer setting, with null island (0,0) as the not-set sentinel. The redundant trailing optional-step dash is now only drawn ahead of the cursor, since behind it the leading indicator already answers.

title: Switching the active profile is only possible by changing which profile launches at startup
summary: Already closed in this shard's working tree; I confirmed it by revert. ProfileSidebar takes an onActivateProfile callback and watches activeEquipmentProfileProvider, so selected and active are distinct states. The footer of a selected-but-not-active profile leads with a primary 'Use This Profile' button (Connect All demotes to outline there — two primaries side by side is no emphasis at all), and the same action heads the per-profile menu. Every card now carries a visible '...' overflow button (profileCardMenuButtonKey) opening the menu that used to be right-click only. The star is relabelled to say what it actually controls: 'Make Startup Default' / 'Startup Default' instead of 'Set as Default', which read as 'use this one' and was the only route anyone found to switching rigs — while silently rewriting every future launch.

title: The optical-train step asks the user to look up a pixel size the driver already reports
summary: Two halves. (a) Pixel size: the camera step now resolves the driver-reported camera name through the shipped camera library (hardwarePresetsService.matchCameraByName) and seeds draft.pixelSizeMicrons, only on an actual camera CHANGE so a hand-typed value survives re-selecting the same camera, and only on a match so an unknown camera prefills nothing rather than guessing. The optical-train field's placeholder stopped saying 'Look this up in your camera spec sheet' and a provenance line under it names where a prefilled number came from ('Filled in from ZWO ASI2600MM Pro in the camera library (IMX571)'), disappearing the moment the user types something else. That code was already in this shard's tree but had NO test; I wrote one. (b) The second camera identification: step 9 offered only 'Choose from camera library', so the operator hunted for the same camera again. It now leads with a one-tap 'Use <camera> settings' button built from the same match, retiring once a preset is applied. Deliberately a tap, not a silent write — gain and offset are the imager's call and the library only recommends.

title: The capture-folder step offers no way to type a path
summary: The folder row was a read-only Text beside a single Browse button, so the native directory chooser was the only way to answer the step — no way to paste `/mnt/nvme/astro` or a UNC share, and the worst possible control on an appliance driven over VNC. Settings > Files & Storage already accepts a typed path for this exact setting (image_output_path), so the wizard that sets it FIRST was the odd one out. The row is now a real TextField that commits on Enter and on focus loss (tabbing away is how people leave a path box), routed through the same existence + writability check the picker's result goes through. The draft is written only once the check passes, so a typo cannot become the answer that unblocks Next; the rejected text stays in the box to be corrected rather than retyped. Remote mode still asks the host, via the existing _verify path. Browse is unchanged.

title: Equipment Settings mixes auto-save and Apply-required sections and repeats its own title
summary: Two parts. (a) The duplicated heading was already removed in this shard's tree (both hosts — the desktop SkotiqDialog and the phone AppBar — already render 'Equipment Settings' directly above the body, and repeating it cost a heading's worth of the dialog's fixed height). (b) The save-model mismatch: Camera/Mount/Focuser save on edit while Built-in Guider alone has Reset/Apply, with nothing saying which is which. Making the guider save on edit would be wrong — it pushes eight interdependent numbers to a guider that may be running right now, and a half-typed max-pulse reaching a live mount is exactly what an atomic Apply prevents — so the difference is now structural rather than remembered: Apply is live ONLY while the fields differ from the config the guider is actually running, a warning-toned 'Not applied yet — press Apply to send these to the guider.' line appears alongside the existing 'Last applied:' line while anything is pending, and the section description states the Apply contract. Typing a value back to its stored value clears the pending state, so the warning never cries wolf.

title: INDI and Alpaca startup discovery default to off after the wizard offered them as scan backends
summary: The driver step's answer is now stored, not thrown away. `OnboardingNotifier.complete()` used to persist only the capture directory; the `selectedDrivers` set steered the wizard's own discovery passes and then died with the draft, while Settings > Equipment > Connection asked the same question again through 'Query INDI/Alpaca on startup' (both default false). A user who found their camera over INDI during onboarding got an app that never queried INDI at launch again. `_persistAppSettings` now writes imageOutputPath, indi_auto_connect and alpaca_auto_discover together — one read-modify-write on a remote host so a second round trip cannot drop the field it did not carry. Both flags are written, not just the true ones, so unticking INDI can take an inherited `true` away. An empty driver set (a draft restored from before the step existed) leaves both toggles alone rather than answering for the user.

title: Discovery says only that no switches or cover calibrators were found, without saying why or what to do
summary: Already closed in this shard's working tree; I confirmed it by revert. Zero-result classes get the same section chrome as every other class — titled header, icon, and an honest '0 found' count instead of one bare italic line — plus a body that names the backends actually searched and any that errored, or 'Not searched yet — run a scan.' before the first scan, and a route to configuring a remote server. The information already existed (the app log recorded 'Discovery complete for Switch: 0 devices, 0 backend errors'); the section that says nothing was found is where it belongs.

title: PHD2 cannot be configured during onboarding unless PHD2 is already running
summary: The onboarding guider step only wrote the guider into the draft inside `if (running)` after a successful socket probe, so a user setting up indoors before launching PHD2 could not record a guider at all - Next dropped the typed host/port and the summary step read '- not set -'. Added an explicit 'Use PHD2' action (plus 'Clear') that persists the draft guider and the phd2Host/phd2Port settings the connect path reads, independent of the probe; Test stays as verification and still selects in one tap when it passes. The selection line is now derived from the draft (not a local flag), so picking a native guider retires it.

title: FocusModelPanel is orphaned - the machine that builds the temperature-compensation model cannot display it
summary: Confirmed: `FocusModelPanel` was constructed nowhere, and Imaging -> Focus carried only Manual Focus and Autofocus, so an operator running autofocus on that very screen had no view of the model those runs build (Settings' focus-model page is remote-only). Mounted the maintained, backend-aware `FocusModelCurveCard` under a 'Temperature Compensation' heading at the foot of the Focus tab - it reads `focusProfileDataProvider`, so it is honest on the rig and on a paired companion alike, and it carries the chart, model quality/R2, prediction and per-filter offsets. Deleted the orphaned `focus_model_panel.dart` (973 lines, zero references, local-only data source that would have shown an empty model over the network) and corrected the stale comment in focus_model_settings.dart that named it. The finding's second half - 'clicking the TC chip in the status bar produced nothing' - is not a defect: status_bar/temperature_and_time.dart:71-95 is a Tooltip-wrapped Container, a passive badge whose tooltip already names slope, R2 and the predicted position; it was never a control, so no drill-in was lost. Mounting the model on Focus is the whole of the real gap.

title: Rotator relative-move strip clips +15 deg off the card with no scroll affordance
summary: Confirmed by measurement: at the 320 px imaging side panel the six step buttons laid out 16..432 inside a card that ends at 304, so +5 straddled the border and +15 sat entirely outside a clipped horizontal SingleChildScrollView with no fade or partial button to hint at it. Replaced the scroll strip with two rows of three Expanded cells (a fade would only have disclosed the problem, not fixed it): every step is drawn inside the card and hit-testable at any panel width, and the buttons get wider rather than narrower - which is what you want for a control you are tapping in the dark. Centred the button label since the box is now wider than its text.

title: Night Narrator ticker produced zero insights across a 65-minute session with 12 frames, an autofocus run and a cooldown
summary: Real, and the cause is structural rather than detector coverage. NarratorTicker returned SizedBox.shrink() whenever sessionStateProvider.dbSessionId was null - and only SequenceExecutor ever calls SessionStateNotifier.startSession, so every manual capture on the Imaging screen is sessionless. NarratorService deliberately keeps running in that case (it binds guiding, weather, autofocus and last-image-stats and persists events with a null session_id), but those rows only ever land in the sessionless bucket that the ticker never read. The strip is now fed from recentNarratorFeedProvider when there is no DB session, and the feed sheet it opens follows the same source so the two cannot contradict each other. The 10-minute rotation window is made mandatory in the sessionless case: that bucket outlives the app, so resting on its newest entry could put a previous night's headline over tonight's canvas.

title: 'Best Targets Tonight' ranks purely by transit altitude, so it recommends obscure galaxies that transit in daylight and pass through the zenith
summary: Confirmed at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/mosaic_targets.dart:184-203 (pre-fix): calculateObjectVisibility per DSO, keep transitAltitude > 30, sort descending on transitAltitude, take 20. Nothing in that key knows where the sun is, and transit altitude is maximised at declination == latitude, so the list was permanently the same band of near-zenith objects and four of five could culminate in daylight on a panel printing sunset/sunrise six rows above. Replaced the key with a new pure module, packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/tonight_ranking.dart: derive tonight's darkness window from the site's own twilight (astronomical night, degrading one band at a time to nautical/civil/sun-down, null under a midnight sun), drop anything with zero usable time above 30 deg inside that window, and rank the rest with the app's OWN night scorer (TargetScoringService.scoreTargetForNight over [darkStart, darkEnd] with minAltitude 30) so the panel can no longer call a target 'best' on a key the planner and the native scheduler disagree with. No new weighting was invented: altitude, moon separation, transit timing, usable hours and airmass are the five axes already shipped and already parity-pinned against Rust. The card now headlines the hours the target is usable in darkness and the moment it peaks INSIDE that window, replacing the shared transit altitude and the daylight transit time; the section carries the subtitle 'Usable hours above 30 deg in darkness, and when each peaks' and the tooltip states the real rule. Twilight and the moon are computed inside the isolate from site+night-date, so the provider still does not depend on any per-minute provider. Measured cost on 12k DSOs: 5707 ms before, 6405 ms after (+12%), same isolate.

title: Search hint badge reads '⌘K' on Linux and Windows, where the shortcut is Ctrl+K
summary: Confirmed: hardcoded Apple Command glyph at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/redesign/command_bar.dart:198 and (as the escape \u2318) packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/search_header.dart:670, on every platform, while the handler accepts Meta OR Control. Added packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/utils/platform_shortcuts.dart with shortcutLabel(key) -> 'Ctrl+K' on Linux/Windows/Android/Fuchsia and '⌘K' on macOS/iOS, exported from the skotiq_ui barrel, and used at both sites.

title: Object search has no exact-designation path: typing a catalogue number returns 175 fuzzy matches
summary: Root cause found in the data, not just the ranking: OpenNGC's Identifiers column is loaded wholesale into DeepSkyObject.catalogIds (packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/catalogs/catalog.dart:198-208), and those cross-identifiers are zero-padded — NGC7107 carries 'PGC 067209', NGC7112 'PGC 067208', IC5118 'PGC 067202', IC728 'UGC 06720'. _scoreMatch scored a typed '6720' as a plain SUBSTRING match against all of them, so every one tied with NGC6720 itself at score 2 and the ONLY thing that put M57 first was the brightness tie-break — i.e. the right answer was luck, and a fainter true match would lose. Added designation-aware ranking in packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/object_search.dart: _splitDesignation parses 'prefix + number' (ignoring zero padding and spacing, and refusing composite survey ids like '2MASX J...' or 'ESO 287-052'), and an exact designation match scores -1, above every _scoreMatch band. A PREFIXED query pins the catalogue ('UGC 6720' answers IC728, not NGC6720); a BARE number is honoured only for M/NGC/IC, deliberately narrow so '6720' cannot promote HD 6720 — that would have replaced one wrong first result with another. This also fixes Enter/fly-to (resolveBest returns results.first).

title: Region detail opens on a viewport-filling empty preview with no empty state; everything informative is below the fold
summary: Confirmed at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/your_sky/region_detail_screen.dart:219-231 (pre-fix): a free AspectRatio(3/2) hero, so on a 1600x900 window it rendered ~1030px tall — taller than the viewport — with a bare grey Container and one icon when there are no folds. Everything that says anything sat below the fold, and the ListView did not even build it. Two cause fixes: the preview is now sized by a LayoutBuilder to min(width * 2/3, 320) so the card's own coordinate line and the sections under it stay on a standard desktop window (BoxFit.cover crops rather than distorts, and on a phone the cap never binds), and the empty state is now words inside the preview ('Nothing imaged here yet' + 'Point a session at this patch of sky and its frames fold in here.'), matching how the parent Your Sky screen handles the same state. Fixing the height exposed a pre-existing RenderFlex overflow in the growth card's empty placeholder — AdaptiveChartContainer.fixed(height: 170) clipped an EmptyState.compact that needs more once narrowed to its 360px column (it would already stripe on a phone today) — so that box became a minHeight floor instead of a fixed height.

title: The Tonight screen hedges about a fact it knows: "may be below your horizon or your location is not set"
summary: Confirmed real. tonightSuggestionsProvider (target_suggestion_provider.dart:100-104) returns an EMPTY list the moment latitude==0 && longitude==0 — before it looks at the sky — so oneTapTargetProvider hands the screen a null pick and the card blamed the horizon, the moon and the location at once, offering only a Refresh that can never succeed. The null-pick branch is now _NoPickCard, which reads the same appSettingsProvider the dashboard/planner/weather surfaces read: unset site -> 'Location not configured' + an 'Open Settings' button routed to /settings?section=location; configured site -> the honest 'Nothing imageable right now' with Refresh kept. The GO path had the same hedge (the controller's NoTonightTargetException default): the screen's pick seam now checks the site itself and throws a message that names it, and the exception's default text was narrowed to the genuinely ambiguous case.

title: "Unattended Autopilot" panel title is permanently truncated
summary: Confirmed real at the cited file, and the first fix for it was INCOMPLETE — I found the residual by measuring instead of trusting. The title was a single ellipsized Text inside a Flexible sharing a Row with the Idle/Running badge, so it rendered 'Unattended Aut…'. An earlier pass changed it to maxLines: 2 and proved that at a 1280 px window, where the panel is 358 px wide. But the panel width is clamp(available * 0.28, 280, 380), so every window from the desktop breakpoint (768) up to ~1170 px puts it on its 280 px FLOOR, and there the Row leaves the title exactly 100.0 logical px (measured: RenderParagraph constraints 0<=w<=100.0, didExceedMaxLines TRUE at text scale 1.0) — less than the word 'Unattended' needs, so two lines were not enough either and the title still clipped, now mid-word and without even an ellipsis. Fixed at the cause the finding itself named: the badge no longer competes for the title's line. The header Row is now Icon + Expanded(Wrap[title, badge]), so the badge stays beside the title while there is room and drops to its own run when there is not, handing the title the panel's full width (measured 214.6 px, didExceedMaxLines false). maxLines: 2 is kept with an explicit TextOverflow.ellipsis, because Flutter's default with maxLines set is TextOverflow.clip — a mid-glyph cut with no cue — which is the wrong way to fail at a very large system text scale.

title: The Object types dialog reflows when a chip is selected, sliding Apply down under the pointer
summary: Confirmed real. The 7 FilterChips sit in a Wrap; Material's default leading checkmark widened the selected chip by 20 logical px, which pushed the Wrap from 2 rows to 3 and moved the Clear/Apply row down. Set showCheckmark: false — selection is already carried by the chip's fill and outline, so the chip is the same width in both states and the action row cannot move. The dialog body was extracted to _showObjectTypeDialog + a @visibleForTesting seam (same pattern as the existing showAngleSliderForTest) because PlannerScreen runs a 1 s sky clock and never settles.

title: Constellation filter is an unsearchable list of 3-letter abbreviations
summary: Confirmed real: _ConstellationDropdown built a DropdownButton with one row per constellation present in tonight's candidates, each labelled 'Constellation: <Abbr>'. Replaced with a _ControlChip that opens a searchable dialog (consistent with every other filter in that row): rows read 'Canes Venatici (CVn)', sorted by full name, with a search field that matches either spelling, a live count of how many constellations tonight's candidates actually cover, and an explicit 'Any constellation' action. The abbreviation->name table was a PRIVATE map inside skotiq_planetarium's OpenNGC catalog; it is now the shared constellation_names.dart (constellationFullName()) and catalog.dart delegates to it, so there is one spelling of 'Canes Venatici' in the app. The finding's ask for 'only constellations with candidates tonight' was already true (availableConstellationsProvider derives from the suggestion set).

title: The Rationale block never names the target it is explaining (and calls a target with no frames a "large unfinished dataset")
summary: Both halves confirmed real. (1) session_optimizer_service.dart:527 gated the line on `primary.dataProgress < 0.25`, and dataProgress is EXACTLY 0.0 when nothing has been captured (target_suggestion_service._calculateDataProgress returns 0.1 for the 'some data, no plan' case), so a target with zero frames was sold as a 'large unfinished dataset' and an 'efficient completion target' in the same block that said 'No data collected yet'. Now gated on `> 0 && < 0.25` and reworded to 'Partially captured already...'. (2) The Rationale SectionHeader read 'Why this plan was chosen' while the numbers under it always belong to plan.primaryTarget — which is NOT the hero card whenever a search or filter leaves a different card on screen. The subtitle now names the target ('Why NGC 6015 was chosen'). I did NOT move the block above the candidate list: that is a layout preference, not a truth defect.

title: Getting a target into the scheduler is a three-deep dead end; every empty state points at another empty state
summary: The dead end is real and I reproduced it in the code: the Add Target sheet (project_dialogs.dart) was a picker over `allDbTargetsProvider` ONLY, and with an empty library it rendered 'No targets in the catalog / Add targets to your library first' with no action — while the only writer of the targets table reachable from the UI was Framing -> Save target (framing_provider.saveTarget) and the plan-tonight sequencer helper. The sheet now also searches the installed sky catalogs (new `installedCatalogSearchProvider` in core — the existing plannerInstalledCatalogSearchProvider deliberately HIDES tonight's candidates, which is exactly backwards for adding one) and creates the library row itself via TargetLibraryService.ensureCatalogTarget (host-aware and dedup-safe), then returns the new id so the caller attaches it to the open project. Rows already in the library are filtered out of the catalog section so an object never appears twice, the row shows type/mag/constellation, and an in-flight add disables the list so a double tap cannot double-create. The empty state now says what to do ('Search for an object by name or catalog id') instead of pointing elsewhere.

title: Scheduler moon avoidance is illumination-only; the app has moon separation everywhere else
summary: Confirmed: TargetConstraintKind had timeWindow / moonIlluminationMax / customHorizon / scheduledWindow and nothing separation-based, so the wizard's 'Moon avoidance' step offered exactly one knob whose semantics are backwards for the common cases (rejects a target 150 deg from a 90% moon, accepts one 10 deg from a 40% moon). Added `moonSeparationMin` end to end: enum + `moonSeparationMinDeg` field + payload encode/decode (payload_json, so no schema migration) + engine evaluation in the same hard-constraint loop as the others, reusing the engine's existing Meeus moon ephemeris and angular-separation helper, with a rejection reason that states the actual separation and the moon's phase. UI: a new 'Moon separation' wizard card + 0-180 deg field + review sentence + row label, and the illumination card was renamed from the over-broad 'Moon avoidance' to 'Moon illumination' now that the pair exists. Default 30 deg. NOT done and left as a decision: the illumination-scaled Lorentzian curve (NINA's) and the missing min-altitude / max-airmass / meridian-side kinds — see the needs-decision item below.

title: Narrowband mixer opens with every channel weight at 0.00, i.e. a palette that renders black
summary: Two causes, both fixed at source. (1) The panel DID adopt a preset in initState, but the masters load asynchronously so initState ran against an EMPTY channel list; when the real Ha/OIII/SII arrived, didUpdateWidget saw a length change and reset the matrix to zeros + 'Custom mix' and never re-adopted. It now re-seeds on the channel SET (masterId:filter keys, so a same-length swap also re-seeds) rather than on the length. (2) _presetApplies used `.any`, so SHO counted as applicable with only Ha present — a Ha+OIII bicolor set auto-adopted a red-less 'SHO'. It now requires the preset's filters to be FULLY covered, which is what makes Ha+OIII resolve to HOO. Added a final floor so no input set can leave a black matrix: when no named palette is satisfied (a lone Ha master, or an NII/Hb-only set) every channel seeds to a 1/1/1 luminance mapping, honestly labelled 'custom'.

title: An unrecognised transient-kind token is presented to the user as a definite 'Dipole' artefact classification, which also silently blocks submission
summary: TransientKind.fromWire fell back to `dipole` for any token it did not recognise, so the card asserted a specific measured morphology the differencing code never reported, and Submit refused on the strength of that invented claim. Added a real `unknown` member (label 'Unclassified'), made fromWire return it, and replaced the dipole-denylist gate with a positive allow-list: new TransientKind.isSubmittable (newSource | pointBrightening | movingStreak) plus TransientKind.submissionBlockedReason, so the class itself owns its refusal wording in ONE place. Both submission surfaces (the First Light candidate card and the shared TransientReportPanel, which the Submit-discovery dialog wraps) now read that getter instead of comparing to dipole, so a future kind cannot silently inherit the dipole message. Conservative gating is unchanged: an unclassified detection is still held back, it is just told the truth about why.

title: The five-rung Science guide is a set of paragraphs, not a ladder you can climb -- every rung opens an explanation and a 'Got it' button with no action
summary: The headline claim is NOT REAL against the current tree, and I found a different, worse defect underneath it. ScienceRungSheet._actions already returns the rung's own CTA when the rung is `ready` (spec.ctaLabel) and 'Jump to it' when it is `done`; only a genuinely LOCKED rung shows 'Got it', which is correct -- that rung cannot be started yet. The finding's evidence is from the shipped 6.1.0 build: the two gate strings it quotes ('Calibrate your sky first so brightness reads true.', 'Find a period - or build out the curve - before exporting.') no longer exist, and the cascade that locked rung 2 was removed in the working tree, so rung 2 is now never locked. What IS broken is rung 1: its CTA 'Run calibration' called onJumpToFieldQuality, which in the populated Science tab merely scrolled to the FIELD QUALITY section -- whose only control grades frames. showDialog(PhotometricCalibrationWizard) was wired ONLY into the all-empty branch of the tab, so the moment the user had any science product at all the calibration wizard became unreachable from anywhere in the app while a button promising it stayed on screen. Renamed the callback to onRunCalibration (named for the action, so a host cannot quietly answer it with a scroll) and wired the populated branch to the wizard.

title: The Submit-discovery dialog opens on TNS even when TNS is unusable and another network is ready
summary: Half of the TNS-default finding is objectively wrong regardless of taste: _format was a hard-coded TransientReportFormat.tns that nothing ever re-evaluated, so an observer with an MPC observatory code (or an AAVSO observer code) but no TNS bot credentials opened the dialog on a DISABLED 'Submit to TNS' with a blocker notice, while the network that would have worked sat behind a chip the notice never pointed at. Added _resolveFormat(), called from build: keep the current selection while it is usable, otherwise move to the first usable one, and when nothing is usable leave the selection alone so the blocker shown belongs to the network being named. The preference order is the shipped one (tns, aavso, mpc), so this only changes which network is shown when the preferred one is blocked -- it does not re-rank the networks. The other half of the finding (should TNS be pre-selected AT ALL, given it is the live, public, irreversible one) is a product call; filed separately below.

title: The 'AstroBin' export produces JSON + Markdown, not the acquisition CSV AstroBin imports, and omits the observation date entirely
summary: Three separable defects, all real. (1) The save dialog asked for a filename and then ignored the extension: exportAstroBinSidecar took the chosen path, stripped its extension and wrote <base>.md + <base>.json, so typing rsr-astrobin.csv produced neither. It is now exportAstroBinAcquisition and the format follows the extension the user chose -- .csv writes AstroBin's acquisition CSV, .json the payload, anything else (including an image path, so the sidecar-beside-the-PNG use still works) the Markdown block. The Markdown block is always written alongside, so choosing the importable format never loses the forum-post text. (2) The metadata had no date at all, and AstroBin requires one on every acquisition row: added AstroBinExportMetadata.date + dateIso, rendered in the Markdown and the JSON, sourced from the imaging session's start time when the result is attached to one (falling back to the run timestamp) so restacking old data does not stamp it with today. (3) The picker now suggests .csv. The CSV emits date,number,duration -- the three fields the importer needs and exactly what a user would otherwise retype. It deliberately does NOT emit a filter column: AstroBin keys filters by equipment-database id, which Skotiq does not hold, and a filter NAME there would break the import rather than fill it in, so the filter stays in the Markdown block.

title: Pre-flight prints the same guider problem twice and both times tells you to connect PHD2, in a build that ships its own native guider
summary: Two halves, one already closed and one still live. The DUPLICATION was fixed by an earlier wave: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/equipment_rules.dart:105-148 now emits per-node 'Guider Not Connected' warnings and keeps the generic 'No Guider Connected' summary as a fallback ONLY when no enabled node can be attributed, with a regression test already in place. The BACKEND-AWARENESS half was still real and is now fixed. The old text said '<node> requires a guider (PHD2)' and, unconditionally, 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.' I confirmed against the Guiding panel that this is bad advice, not just imprecise: desktop_sections.dart:230 only renders a Connect button when `isPhd2Guider` is true, and for any other backend it renders an 'Equipment' button (desktop_sections.dart:252) that navigates away. This build discovers and connects a 'Built-in Multi-Star Guider' (native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/discovery.rs:779), so an operator running the native guider was sent to a panel with no Connect button on it. The rule now drops PHD2 from the description and routes the hint through a new `_guiderResolutionHint(GuiderState)`: PHD2 selected -> 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.'; another backend selected -> 'Connect <device name> in the Equipment panel.'; nothing selected -> 'Connect a guider in the Equipment panel - the built-in multi-star guider, or PHD2.' The hint is computed once and shared by both the per-node warnings and the fallback summary, so the two cannot drift.

title: Node palette search ranks Smart Exposure above the node literally named 'Dither' when you search 'Dither'
summary: The location named in the finding is already correct - packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/node_palette.dart:54 and .../sequencer_screen_parts/node_palette.dart:35 both route through the shared `rankNodePaletteMatches` (node_palette_search.dart), which scores exact name 100 / prefix 80 / name-substring 60 / description 20 and hoists the best-scoring category, with tests in sequencer_jank_p3_test.dart. But a THIRD node-palette search box was still running the old, unranked filter: the Insert Above / Insert Below picker reached from the tree's right-click menu (`_InsertNodePicker` in sequence_tree_context_menu.dart) filtered on `name.contains(q) || description.contains(q)` and rendered survivors in catalogue order, so typing 'Dither' there still put Smart Exposure first - the exact failure the finding describes, on the surface a user reaches when they right-click to insert a node at a specific slot. Moved it onto the shared ranker.

title: Continue Session reports '0 minutes integration' for a session that has 12s of integration on the card behind it
summary: Real, and the finding's `screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart` unit is the wrong file - the Progress row is built by packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart:324-340 (the 'Continue Session' dialog) and formatted by `_formatIntegration(double hours)` at :134, which returned `'${hours.toStringAsFixed(1)} hours'` above 1h and `'${(hours*60).round()} minutes'` below it. 12s = 0.0033h rounds to 0, so a run with four real light frames on disk announced '0 minutes integration'. Fixed at the cause by giving the app ONE integration formatter: new `formatIntegrationSeconds` / `formatIntegrationHours` in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/utils/duration_format.dart (h/m/s, rounding to whole seconds first so 59.6s reads '1m 0s' not '60s', and clamping negative/non-finite to '0s'). `ParsedRunStats.formatDuration` - the formatter the dashboard's last-night recap card, the history tab and the post-session dialog already render - now delegates to it, and the Continue Session dialog calls it too, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about the same run. 12s now reads '12s' in both places.

title: A node can only be reordered by drag; the node context menu offers just Duplicate and Delete
summary: The finding's inventory of the menu is stale - the right-click menu already carried eight entries (Skip to here, Insert Above, Insert Below, Duplicate, Group into Sequential, Group into Parallel, Disable/Enable, Delete), and Move Up / Move Down already existed in the row's kebab 'More Actions' menu (node_item.dart:937-962), so drag was NOT the only route. What was real: the right-click menu itself had no reorder, which is the menu an operator opens when they want to move a node; and the in-code justification for that split cited a 'Shift+Up / Shift+Down keyboard shortcut wired in sequence_tree_shortcuts.dart' that does not reorder anything - kSequenceTreeShortcuts:68-71 binds Shift+Arrow to EXTEND THE SELECTION. Added Move Up / Move Down to SequenceTreeContextMenu, going through the same `moveNode(id, parentId, index)` call the kebab and drag-drop use (one undo entry shape, one reindex path), disabled with an explanatory tooltip on the root and at either end of a sibling list. Corrected the false comment in node_item.dart rather than leaving a note that misdescribes the keymap.

title: PolarAlignmentNode cannot be added to a sequence - it is absent from the palette
summary: Confirmed real and objectively wrong: PolarAlignmentNode has a model (alignment_and_dome.dart:319), a properties editor (_motion_rich.dart:978), serialisation on both the file and repository paths, a time estimate, validation coverage, a registered Rust executor (native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/node/registry.rs:114) and is emitted by SmartNightService - but no palette entry existed in any category, so the only way to get one into a sequence was to have Smart Night generate it or to hand-edit a file. Added a 'Polar Alignment' item to the Mount category next to Meridian Flip. Its isNorth follows the observer latitude the same way SmartNightService derives it (sequence_emitter.dart:310), so a southern-hemisphere operator does not silently get a node that rotates about the north celestial pole.

title: Palette search with no matches renders a completely blank panel
summary: Confirmed. Every palette surface fed rankNodePaletteMatches straight into a ListView.builder, so an empty result rendered zero children and the body went blank between the search field and the help tip - indistinguishable from a failed load. There are THREE such surfaces, not one: the toolbox Nodes tab (sequencer_screen_parts/node_palette.dart), and both branches of the standalone NodePalette (desktop sidebar + mobile add-node sheet). Added a shared NodePaletteEmptyState that names the query back ('No nodes match "polar"'), says what to try, and carries a working Clear search button; wired into all three.

title: Validation badges on the sequence header are not clickable, so the only way to read '1 error' is to press Start
summary: Confirmed: _ValidationBadges rendered plain Containers with no gesture handler, the Builder has no issues panel, and the only route to the issue text was the pre-flight dialog - i.e. pressing the button that arms the rig. Badges are now an InkWell ('Show sequence issues') opening a read-only SequenceIssuesDialog that lists the live validation issues errors-first with title, description and resolution hint, and selects the offending node when an issue names one. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the finding's second half, reclassifying 'Empty Sequence'/'No Exposures' from error to info. Those two genuinely block Start, so error is the honest severity; softening it would make the badge lie in the other direction. The real complaint - that you could not read what the badge meant - is what is fixed.

title: Live Stacking's explanatory helper text is truncated to one ellipsised line
summary: Confirmed, and the cause is not in that file. Flutter's InputDecoration.helperMaxLines defaults to null, which its own docs define as 'soft line breaks are truncated with an ellipse' - the helper Text is built with overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis and maxLines: helperMaxLines (input_decorator.dart:397-402). Nothing in the app ever set it, so EVERY helperText in the app ellipsised, not just these two. Set helperMaxLines: 4 once in SkotiqTheme's inputDecorationTheme, which is the single factory behind dark/light/redNight/accent themes. All 15 helperText call sites in the repo live in scrolling property panels or dialogs, so wrapping costs nothing and no layout is forced taller than its container.

title: Two different things are called Save, two different things are called Templates, and the tab names collide
summary: Both halves confirmed. (1) The toolbar floppy was labelled 'Save Sequence' and calls SequenceFileService.exportSequence - an OS file chooser writing a .nsq - while the Sequences tab's 'Save Current' is what persists into the app. Relabelled to 'Export Sequence File...' (and the force-save dialog's operationName with it). (2) The Builder's left panel is the 'Snippets' tab, its import tooltip already said 'Import snippet from file...', it stores TemplateSnippets - and it titled itself 'Templates', the name of a top-level tab holding whole saved sequences. The panel now says 'Snippets' in both its wide and compact headers, searches 'Search snippets...', and its help/tooltip copy says snippet. This is a self-contradiction inside one panel, not a taste call.

title: Filter is a free-text field with no binding to the wheel; a typo becomes a 2am run failure
summary: Half of this was already true in the tree and half was a real gap. NOT real: 'Change Filter's Properties offers a plain text box' - _FilterChangeProperties (_capture_rich.dart:103-160) renders a DropdownButton over the ACTIVE PROFILE's filterNames, falls back to free text only when the profile declares none, and already surfaces a stored-but-missing name as an explicit '(not in profile)' row plus a warning. REAL: 'validate the name against the profile at build time rather than at run time'. FilterInWheelRule only runs when a filter wheel is CONNECTED (filter_rules.dart:43-46), which is never true while a sequence is built in daylight - so 'Ha' vs 'H-alpha' survived the builder. Added FilterInProfileRule: when no wheel is connected and the active profile declares filters, every enabled ExposureNode.filter and FilterChangeNode.filterName must match one (case-insensitively) or it warns, naming the node. Silent when the profile lists nothing (nothing to check against) and silent when a wheel is connected (the live wheel is the better authority). Refactored the shared node walk into one _filterUses helper so the two rules cannot drift.

title: Loop defaults to 1 iteration and Conditional defaults to 'Always Execute' - both are no-ops out of the box
summary: Confirmed: the palette builds LoopNode() (conditionType count, repeatCount 1) and ConditionalNode() (conditionType always), so both nodes arrive doing exactly nothing and the tree shows no sign of it. Added NoOpLogicNodeRule, which flags a count-type Loop at <= 1 iteration and a Conditional set to Always, at INFO severity, with affectedNodeId set so the tree paints the node and the header badge counts it - and, thanks to the badge fix in this same batch, the operator can now read it in one click. I deliberately did NOT invent a better default count: 2? 10? is unknowable from here, and picking one would silently impose taste on every sequence built from the palette while ALSO not fixing Conditional (which has no 'unset' value in its enum at all). Surfacing the no-op at build time is the fix that is available without deciding what the operator meant. If the owner wants a non-1 default, that is a one-line follow-up in node_palette.dart.

title: Mosaic preview shows only 5 of 9 panel numbers for a 3x3 grid and hides the centre panel's number under the drag handle
summary: Half confirmed, half not reproducible. NOT REPRODUCIBLE: 'only 5 of 9 numbers render'. A widget test over the real MosaicWizardDialog at the default 3x3 grid finds all nine numbers, 1-9, inside the planner - so the missing ones in the screenshot were low-contrast reading, not absent widgets. CONFIRMED and structural: the drag-centre handle is drawn at exactly centerPx (visual_planner.dart:291-305) and every panel number was Center()-ed in its cell, so the middle panel of ANY odd grid had its number under an opaque 12 px accent dot - it can never have been legible. Moved the number to the panel's top-left corner as a small badge with its own scrim: it clears the handle for every grid parity, and the scrim keeps it readable over the neighbouring panels' translucent overlap fills. Added a ValueKey to the handle so the geometry is assertable.

title: Starters tab says 'copy one into your current sequence' but the action replaces the whole sequence
summary: Confirmed - the app stating something untrue. _useStarter calls CurrentSequenceNotifier.loadSequence, which replaces the loaded sequence outright (it only pauses to confirm when the current one is dirty). 'Copy into' is the one reading that would make an operator tap it with work already loaded. The caption now reads 'Bundled, ready-to-run sample sequences. Loading one replaces your current sequence.' and the button reads 'Replace with this starter'.

title: UI scale dropdown truncates its own selected value to 'Extra Lar...' at large UI scale
summary: SettingsDropdown now measures its labels with a TextPainter at the ambient text scale and grows from the design width to fit the widest one, capped by the width the row actually offers (LayoutBuilder), so it can never trade an ellipsis for an overflow stripe. The widest label is used rather than the selected one so the control does not resize under the pointer. SkotiqDropdown gained `labelStyle` and `chromeWidth` constants and now paints with `labelStyle`, so the measurement and the painting cannot drift apart. Root cause: 'UI scale' is applied as a TEXT scaler in app.dart (_calculateUiScaleFactor -> combinedTextScale), so at 1.4x every label grows 40% inside a 140 px box that does not — the defect was latent for every SettingsDropdown, not just this row.

title: 'Reset All to 0 deg' wipes an imported horizon with no confirmation, one click from the Import button
summary: Reset now runs through _resetHorizon, which asks first whenever there is anything to lose — a destructive ConfirmDialog naming exactly what goes ('The imported survey of 36 samples, and the eight sector values below it, will be replaced by a flat 0 degree horizon') and stating that Skotiq does not keep the file it was imported from, so it cannot be undone. A hand-edited mask (any sector above 0) is guarded the same way. An already-flat horizon still resets with no dialog, so the guard is not noise on the case where nothing is at risk.

title: Storage path fields look like editable text inputs but silently ignore typing
summary: SettingsPathInput takes an optional onPathEntered. Where it is supplied the box is a real TextField that commits on Enter AND on focus loss (tabbing away is how people leave a path box) and snaps back to the stored value if the write is refused; where it is not, the box is rendered as a plain label with no border, fill or placeholder, so it stops inviting typing that goes nowhere. Files & Storage supplies it for Image output and Sequences, validated rather than trusted: empty and relative paths are refused with the reason, remote mode still blocks the host-only keys, and a folder this machine cannot create is confirmed ('Store anyway' / Cancel) instead of being silently accepted — which keeps the finding's own use case (a NAS or UNC share that is not mounted yet, unreachable from any directory picker) working without letting a 3am typo become a night of frames written nowhere. The probe is behind storageDirectoryProbeProvider so the flow is drivable without touching disk.

title: At a ~900px window the status bar shows three identical 'Disconnected' chips with no device names
summary: The dense (sub-1280 px) pill now shows the device NAME while the device is disconnected and its live value once it is connected, instead of always dropping the label. Nothing is lost: disconnected is already carried by the muted dot, the muted icon and the tooltip ('Mount: Disconnected'), whereas 'Disconnected' repeated three times carried nothing at all. It also buys width back rather than spending it — 'Camera' is half the length of 'Disconnected' — which mitigates the same finding's complaint that the Focus chip gets scrolled out of the group.

title: Files & Storage refuses to name the application data folder, so a user cannot find their own database, logs or backups
summary: The 'Database and logs' row now resolves the real directory (applicationDataPathProvider -> resolveDefaultDatabaseFile().parent) and shows it, with the same 'Open folder' / 'Copy path' action the Backups row one line below already had, and a sentence saying what is in there (skotiq.db, the logs folder, quarantined/recovered database files) and that this is what to attach to a bug report. When SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR is actually set the row says the folder is pinned by it; on a normal desktop install that line is not shown, because it would be noise.

title: Settings search returns section names only - it never shows or scrolls to the row that matched
summary: The matcher now returns SettingsSearchResult(section, matchingRows) instead of throwing the row information away: matchingSettingsRows keeps every indexed row title that answers ALL query tokens, shortest first (short entries are the ones that really are a row's name), up to three per section. Desktop and mobile both render those rows indented under their section as their own tappable results. Tapping one opens the section AND targets the row: settings_screen publishes the title through a new SettingsRowHighlight inherited widget, and SettingRow reveals itself when it is the target — Scrollable.ensureVisible after the frame that placed it, plus a primary tint that clears after 4 s so it reads as a pointer and not as a selected state. Typing 'Alpaca' now shows 'Alpaca Server Address' and 'Query Alpaca on startup' and takes you to either.

title: The latitude and longitude fields silently discard any coordinate that is not already decimal degrees
summary: The half of 'Location has no place search' that was objectively wrong rather than a matter of taste, and which the previous pass on this findings file recommended but did not implement. Latitude/Longitude were plain SettingsNumberInputs whose digits-only inputFormatter rejected every non-numeric keystroke, so a site held in degrees-minutes-seconds — what a GPS handset, a topo map and most club site lists give you — could not be typed, and PASTING one was a silent no-op: the box did not change and nothing was said. SettingsNumberInput gained an optional `parse` hook which, when supplied, both replaces double.tryParse on commit AND lifts the digits-only formatter (the formatter is what made the paste silent) and switches the phone keyboard to text so N/S/E/W are reachable. parseSiteAngle() in location_settings.dart reads decimal degrees, D M S, D:M:S, degree/prime/double-prime marks, d/m/s unit letters and a leading or trailing hemisphere letter; it disambiguates a trailing 's' (South vs the seconds unit) by whether the string also uses d/m unit letters. It REFUSES rather than guesses — out of range, more than three components, a fraction before the last component, minutes/seconds >= 60, or a sign contradicting the hemisphere all return null, which makes the field snap back to the stored site instead of inventing one. On commit the field normalises to decimal degrees, so the operator sees that '44 3 29 N' was read as 44.058056 and not 4432.9. Both row subtitles now name the accepted forms; the search-index generator only indexes `title:`, so no regeneration was needed.

title: Enter does not submit the profile dialogs, so the fastest path through them is mouse-only
summary: Confirmed and fixed at the cause. Both profile dialogs are a single auto-focused, pre-filled TextField with no onSubmitted, so the focused field swallowed Return and the only way to commit was to leave the keyboard. Added textInputAction: TextInputAction.done + onSubmitted: (_) => _submit() to the Create dialog's name field (screen_shell.dart:777) and the Duplicate dialog's name field (screen_shell.dart:905). _submit is the same method the primary button calls, so nothing is bypassed: an empty/whitespace name is still refused with the inline error, and a duplicate name that collides with an existing profile is still rejected. The Create dialog's description field is deliberately untouched — it is maxLines: 2, where Return is a newline.

title: Import failures are reported as raw Dart exception text ('Import failed: FormatException: Unexpected character (at character 1)')
summary: Confirmed; the finding's file was wrong (the import handler is screen_shell.dart's _importProfiles, not profile_controls.dart, which contains only presentational widgets). Fixed both halves the finding names. (1) Exports now identify themselves: exportProfileToJson and exportAllProfilesToJson both write profileExportEnvelope() = {format: 'skotiq.equipment-profile', version: 2, exportDate, profiles: [...]}, so the importer has something to check against. (2) profilesFromExportDocument() accepts every shape already on disk (the new envelope, the pre-envelope {version, profiles} batch, a bare single-profile map, a bare list) and rejects everything else in operator prose, never a Dart toString: a non-JSON file is told it 'is not a Skotiq equipment profile — it is not JSON at all', unrelated JSON that it 'contains no profile data', another product's export is named back, and a document whose format version is newer than this build gets 'exported by a newer version of Skotiq ... Update Skotiq and import it again' instead of being half-parsed into a wrong profile. (3) parseExportedProfile() restates each field-level rejection naming the profile ('Skotiq could not import "Widefield": focalLength must be non-negative.') or its position. (4) The screen substitutes the picked file's name (describeProfileImportFailure), so the message names the file the operator chose.

title: About shows 6.1.0 but drops the build number, and System Information omits everything a support ticket needs
summary: Half was already closed by an earlier wave, verified in the tree rather than assumed: about_settings.dart already renders 'Version ${version} (build ${buildNumber})'. The System Information half was real — Platform / OS Version / Dart Version and nothing else, none of which distinguishes two installs of the same release, and no way to hand any of it to a bug report except by retyping. The card now renders systemInformationProvider: Skotiq version+build, Platform, OS version, Dart, 'Connected to' (this computer, or the named imaging host — a remote client's facts were otherwise indistinguishable from a local one's), the database schema version, and the resolved data folder; plus a Copy button that puts the block on the clipboard as 'label: value' lines. The data folder is a separate FutureProvider on purpose: path_provider is a platform channel, and awaiting it inside the main provider put the whole card behind a spinner — which hung every pre-existing About test's pumpAndSettle until I split it. I did not add the Rust bridge version: nothing in the Dart layer exposes one today, and inventing a number for a support ticket is worse than omitting it.

title: Replay & Debug is written for the developer who built it: a lowercase title sentence and two user-facing dialogs that name a database table
summary: Confirmed on all four counts. (1) The page header is now 'Replay & Debug' — matching the settings entry that navigates to it, which already read 'Replay & Debug' — with a sentence-cased description of what the retention window is for, replacing 'decision-log retention + cleanup for the retrospective Replay screen.'. (2) 'persisted to the sequence_decisions table' and 'This deletes every row in the sequence_decisions table' are gone; no user-facing string in the page names a SQL table. (3) The confirmation states the magnitude before asking for consent: 'This deletes all 3 recorded decisions, for every past run.' That needed a real count, so ReplayDebugService.countAll() was added, GET /api/sequencer/replay-debug/decisions/count now counts every row when runId is omitted (existing per-run callers are unaffected), NetworkBackend.replayCountAllDecisions() reads it, and ReplayDebugSettingsController.countAllHistory() returns null when the authority cannot say — an older host answers 400 — in which case the dialog says 'every decision Skotiq has recorded' rather than inventing a number. (4) The dialog is now the shared ConfirmDialog with isDestructive: true, so 'Clear history' is the filled destructive button and Cancel is a ghost, matching the profile-delete dialog.

title: Seven paired devices are all called 'Android companion' with no way to tell them apart before revoking
summary: Fixed the part that is objectively wrong rather than a matter of taste: the host has always stored what each token is allowed to do (paired_devices.auth_grant_spec, default 'control', 'admin' for a device that asked for it) and the list never showed it, so the row holding admin looked identical to a view-only one — at exactly the moment you are deciding what to revoke. Each row now carries an access badge beside the device-type label: 'Full access' (admin, warning-coloured), 'Can control the rig', 'View only', or 'Custom access' for the fine-grained `resource:level,...` form, with the raw spec on the tooltip. No new data is collected and no wire format changed; the value was already in the model the screen renders. The rest of the finding (rename, last-seen IP, real device model) is a product decision and is reported separately below, not implemented.

title: Paired devices cannot be renamed, and nothing records which device on the network a row is
summary: Revisited and built option (b), the rename, which this entry had itself recommended; options (a) client-reported model and (c) last-client-IP remain genuinely open and are recorded below. On reflection the rename is not a matter of taste: paired_devices_table.dart:8 documents device_name as 'Device name provided during pairing (e.g. "John's iPhone")', but the only client that ever writes it sends a per-platform constant (apps/mobile/lib/services/mobile_pairing_service.dart:49-57 -> 'Android companion' for every Android device, forever), so the schema's own stated intent is unreachable by any operator action and revoking the handset you sold stays guesswork no matter how carefully you read the rows. Added PairingDatabase.renamePairedDevice (returns rows changed so a caller can tell a rename that hit nothing from one that landed), TokenManager.renameDevice (session token, grant and expiry untouched, so naming a device never disturbs one that is mid-run), PairingNotifier.renameDevice (same _enqueue/generation/backend-authority discipline as revoke and delete; refuses an empty name; on a row that has since been deleted it refreshes the list and reports failure rather than claiming a rename), and a 'Rename Device' row-menu action opening a one-field dialog that opens focused on the current name, commits on Return, and disables Save while the field is blank. Nothing new is collected, no wire format changed, and the write is to the same host database the list already reads.

title: 'Restore' asks you to restart the app afterwards but does not offer to, and nothing on the screen stays to remind you
summary: Confirmed and fixed at the cause: a permanent condition was being announced in a transient message. Both restore paths (a listed backup, and an imported file) now set a persistent banner on the Backup & Restore screen — 'Restart required' plus 'Restored N items. Restart Skotiq before the next run — until then this app is showing the state it had before the restore.' (or the imaging-host wording in remote mode) — which stays until the operator presses Dismiss. The snackbar is gone, so there is one message, not two. I did not add a 'Restart now' button: relaunching a Flutter desktop process from inside itself means spawning the executable and exiting, which is a real risk to take on a machine that may have a rig connected, and it is not needed to close the defect (the operator now cannot lose the message).

title: A 426 MB abandoned GLADE download sat in the catalog directory for six weeks with nothing in the UI acknowledging it
summary: Confirmed as a real leak, with a narrower cause than the finding assumed. The download path already deletes its own `.partial` in a `finally` on both cancel and error (annotation_catalog_io.dart, legacy_catalog_io.dart), so a normal failure cleans up; what nothing handles is a process that dies mid-download — a crash, a kill, or a power cut — which is exactly how a 407 MiB leftover survives six weeks. Fixed at the cause: CatalogManager.initialize() now sweeps `*.partial` files in the catalog directory and logs the bytes reclaimed. That is safe and complete rather than cosmetic, because a partial is never resumable (each attempt opens the temp path with openWrite, which truncates), so there is nothing to offer to resume and nothing lost by deleting it; and the sweep runs at startup, before any download this process starts, so it cannot race one. I deliberately did NOT add a 'Partial download: 407 MB — Resume / Discard' card as the finding suggested: 'Resume' would be a lie about a file that is always thrown away, and 'Discard' is a button for a condition the app can simply not leave behind.

title: Radar timeline opens on the OLDEST frame, so the Weather screen shows two-hour-stale cloud by default
summary: Real and objectively wrong. WeatherScreen held `int _currentFrameIndex = 0` and handed it straight to the scrubber, so first paint sat on frame 1 of N — up to two hours behind the NOW marker the scrubber itself paints at the far right — until the operator dragged or pressed play. Fixed at the cause: the screen now holds `int? _selectedFrameIndex` where null means 'nobody has scrubbed', and the rendered index resolves to `latestObservedRadarFrameIndex(frames)`, a new documented pure helper in radar_timeline_scrubber.dart. It returns the last frame with isForecast false, not simply the last frame, because RainViewer appends nowcast tiles and Open-Meteo / MET Norway append future hours (rainviewer_radar_provider.dart:131-138, openmeteo_cloud_provider.dart:160) — opening on those would show predicted cloud as if it had been measured. All-forecast lists fall back to index 0, the frame nearest to now. Because the state is null until the operator touches the scrubber, the timeline also keeps tracking the live edge across the screen's 5-minute refresh instead of drifting; once they scrub, their choice sticks (still clamped). The finding's second suggestion — repurposing skip-forward to jump to NOW — was NOT done: it is the 'Next frame' step control, and stealing it would remove the only way to step the loop forward.

title: The Slew split-button's primary half does nothing - every slew costs two clicks through a menu
summary: Real and objectively wrong. The filled 'Slew' half was a costume: the entire visual child sat inside IgnorePointer with `onPressed: enabled ? () {} : null`, and PopupMenuButton owned the whole hit area, so clicking the word 'Slew' opened a menu whose first entry was also 'Slew'. The commonest action on the control cost two clicks and a menu traversal, and the affordance lied about what the left half did. Fixed at the cause: the widget is now an actual split button — a Row of SkotiqButton (onPressed runs _handleSlewMode(SlewMode.slew) directly) beside a PopupMenuButton carrying only the chevron. Both call sites (mount_tab.dart:431 manual GoTo, framing_actions_panel.dart:316 'Slew to Target') keep their layout; the chevron gained symmetric padding so it is a real tap target instead of a bare 16px glyph. Safety is unchanged: every entry point still runs through _handleSlewMode, so the below-horizon confirm gate, the single-flight latch and the backend-revision guard all still apply — proven by the existing horizon-gate tests, which now drive the primary half. Accessibility: the old wrapper Semantics is gone because SkotiqButton publishes its own button/enabled/label node and is keyboard-focusable; the chevron is wrapped in Semantics(label: 'More slew options') because PopupMenuButton contributes only a 'Show menu' tooltip and would otherwise reach a screen reader unnamed.

title: Enabling Morning Report in the widget picker adds nothing and gives no explanation
summary: CockpitMorningReport returned SizedBox.shrink() when sequenceRunsProvider was empty, so ticking the picker checkbox produced no tile anywhere and read as a broken toggle. It now renders the same _ReportStatusCard shell the loading/error states use, headed 'No completed runs yet' and saying what will appear there once a sequence finishes — the shape Storage and Last Run already use.

title: Polar alignment reports error in raw arcseconds ("1800.0 arcseconds", "Up 2287.9\""), which no one adjusting a wedge can read
summary: Added one shared formatter, formatPolarError, that follows the magnitude the way NINA/SharpCap do: arcseconds with a decimal under 1', arcmin+arcsec under 1 degree, degrees+arcmin+arcsec above that, sign preserved, non-finite rendered as '--'. Wired into every readout that previously printed a raw arcsecond count: the Adjust Mount az/alt/total tiles and its threshold caption, the right-rail Azimuth/Altitude/Total tiles, the completion headline (both the 'Final error' and 'Still N off' branches), the Before/After summary boxes, the history rows, and the All-Sky reticle caption. The fixed 30"/60"/120" ring labels on the bullseye were deliberately left in arcseconds — that is the regime where the arcsecond IS the unit.

title: The History button in the polar alignment header appears to do nothing — the panel it opens is off-screen below the config column
summary: The screen now owns the configuration column's ScrollController, and toggling History ON animates that column to the panel it just appended (and selects the Settings tab on the compact layout, where the column is a tab). The button also carries a tooltip saying where the panel appears. The panel stays where it is structurally — the defect was that the toggle's only effect was below the fold, not where the panel lives.

title: Polar alignment config controls stay visually enabled during a run but silently ignore clicks
summary: The controls were already genuinely disabled (every callback is `isRunning ? null : ...`), so the defect was purely that nothing said so: SegmentedButton.styleFrom used the same surfaceAlt for enabled and disabled, so the column kept full contrast.
